heroText: Conakry is Guinea's capital, stretched along the narrow Kaloum peninsula into the Atlantic with a humid, tropical feel. First-time visitors should tour the Grand Mosque of Conakry, one of West Africa's largest, browse the National Museum of Guinea for masks and instruments, and take a short boat ride to the Iles de Los. Ahmed Sekou Toure International Airport connects the city to the wider region and coastal getaways.

areas.name: Kaloum
areas.text: Kaloum is the peninsula tip forming Conakry's historic centre, with government buildings, the port and the National Museum within walking distance.

areas.name: Dixinn
areas.text: Dixinn is a leafy residential and university district east of Kaloum, offering a quieter base with easy access into the centre.

areas.name: Ratoma
areas.text: Ratoma is Conakry's embassy and business hotel district, popular for its newer hotels, restaurants and proximity to the airport road.

airports.name: Ahmed Sekou Toure International Airport (CKY)
airports.search: Ahmed Sekou Toure International Airport, Conakry, Guinea
airports.text: Ahmed Sekou Toure International Airport sits in Ratoma, north of the city centre; traffic on the coastal road can slow transfers into Kaloum.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Ahmed Sekou Toure International Airport (CKY) and central Conakry before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in Ratoma for newer hotels close to the airport and embassies, or Dixinn for a quieter, leafy stay near the university. Kaloum suits visitors who want to be within walking distance of the port, museum and government district.
hotelIntro: Conakry hotel choice depends mostly on purpose: Ratoma offers the newest business hotels near the airport, Dixinn suits quieter longer stays, and Kaloum keeps you closest to the port, museum and historic centre.
rentalCars: A rental car with a driver helps for trips to the Iles de Los or Kindia, but taxis are the easier way to get around central Conakry itself.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Ratoma for airport convenience and newer hotels, or Kaloum for walking distance to the museum, port and government district.

travelTips.title: Traffic
travelTips.text: The coastal road linking the airport, Ratoma and Kaloum can be slow at peak hours, so build extra time into transfers.

travelTips.title: Cash
travelTips.text: Carry Guinean francs in cash for markets and taxis, since card acceptance is limited outside the larger hotels.

travelTips.title: Boat trips
travelTips.text: Book a boat to the Iles de Los a day ahead, since departures depend on tides and available fishing boats.

history.text: In 1885, the two island villages of Conakry and Boubinet had fewer than 500 inhabitants.
The city was essentially founded after Britain ceded the island to France in 1887.

Conakry became the capital of French Guinea in 1904, and prospered as an export port, particularly after a railway (now closed) to Kankan opened up the interior of the country for the large-scale export.
In the decades after Guinea gained independence in 1958, the population of Conakry boomed, from 50,000 inhabitants in 1958 to 600,000 in 1980 to more than 3.4 million today.

In 1970, conflict between Portuguese forces and the belligerent PAIGC independence campaigners in neighbouring Portuguese Guinea (now Guinea-Bissau) spilled into the Republic of Guinea when a group of 350 Portuguese troops and Guinean loyalists.
According to human rights groups, 157 people died during the 2009 Guinea protest when the military junta opened fire against tens of thousands of protesters in the city on 28 September 2009.

history.label: Civic role
history.text: The city's small land area and relative isolation from the mainland, while an advantage to its colonial founders, has created an infrastructural burden since independence.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Camp Boiro, a feared concentration camp during the rule of Sekou Touré, was located in Conakry.
